version.changelog:
claw-cleaning 1.0.6 changelog:

- Switched integration from the MCP server to a direct REST API over HTTPS for all booking and availability actions.
- Updated connection instructions: now uses public, unauthenticated REST endpoints (`/availability`, `/bookings/initiate`, `/bookings/status`).
- Clarified error handling: added HTTP status codes, API error messages, and JSON request/response formats.
- Improved workflow steps and endpoint usage examples for clarity and precision.
- Removed references to streamable HTTP and MCP connectors; updated technical notes throughout.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: claw-cleaning
Version: 1.0.6

The skill is a straightforward API wrapper for booking apartment cleaning services in San Francisco via the claw.cleaning domain. It follows a well-defined workflow including availability checks, explicit user confirmation before booking, and clear error handling. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, unauthorized system access, or malicious prompt injection.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent: it documents a simple, unauthenticated REST booking flow, asks for the customer info needed to make bookings, and does not request unrelated credentials or install anything.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (book apartment cleanings in SF) match the instructions and endpoints in SKILL.md. The skill only requires calling claw.cleaning endpoints (availability, initiate booking, status). There are no unexpected environment variables, binaries, or install steps.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to checking availability, collecting customer details (date/time/hours/address/name/email), and posting bookings. They do not instruct the agent to read local files, access unrelated env vars, or reach out to other endpoints. Note: the skill will transmit customer PII (full street address, name, email) to the external domain https://claw.cleaning as part of normal operation — this is expected for a booking skill but is a privacy consideration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. This is the lowest install risk (nothing written to disk, no third-party packages downloaded).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no credentials or environment variables (proportionate). However, it requires collecting personal data (address, name, email) and will send that data to an external, unauthenticated API over HTTPS; users should be aware of that data sharing and confirm consent before sending PII.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent system privileges or modify other skills or system config. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but there is no elevated persistence requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent and limited to booking flow, but before installing consider: (1) confirm you trust the external domain https://claw.cleaning and the operator (no homepage or publisher info is provided here); (2) the skill will send customer PII (address, name, email) to that third party — ensure customers consent and that your privacy requirements are met; (3) the endpoints are unauthenticated, so verify the service's legitimacy and data-retention/privacy policy if possible; (4) enforce the SKILL.md safety rule to always show a full booking preview and get explicit confirmation before POSTing (to avoid accidental bookings); (5) test the API with non-sensitive data first and monitor for unexpected behavior (spam bookings, excess calendar invites); and (6) if you need stronger guarantees, request the publisher provide a homepage, contact/ownership verification, or an authenticated API with documented provenance.
